title: Pronoun Declension 6: Mixed Review and the Reflexive Pronoun себя
titleRussian: Склонение местоимений 6: повторение и возвратное местоимение себя
description: Synthesis of the five lessons in this track plus the reflexive pronoun себя (oneself), which has no nominative and uses one form across the acc / gen, separate forms for dat (себе), instr (собой), and prep (о себе).
descriptionRussian: Повторение пяти уроков трека плюс возвратное местоимение себя (без именительного; винительный и родительный совпадают, дательный себе, творительный собой, предложный о себе).
intro: One genuinely new word arrives in the last lesson. Себя points back at whoever the subject is, and it does not care who that is: a single set of forms covers every person, gender and number, which makes it the simplest pronoun in Russian. The rest of the lesson mixes everything from the previous five.
rules: The reflexive pronoun себя has four case forms: acc / gen себя, dat себе, instr собой, prep о себе. It has NO nominative because it never functions as a subject.
Use себя whenever the object refers back to the subject. Use the regular personal pronoun when the object is a different person.
Себя is invariant for person, gender, and number. The subject's identity does not change the form.

Свой / своя / своё / свои is the possessive that points back to the subject. Свой declines exactly like мой / твой. Use свой instead of мой / твой / его when the possessor is the subject of the clause.
examples: Я знаю себя. (I know myself.) Subject = я, object refers back to subject; use the reflexive acc себя.
Маша готовит себе кофе. (Masha is making herself coffee.) Subject = Маша, indirect object = self; use the reflexive dat себе.
Антон гордится собой. (Anton is proud of himself.) Subject = Антон, instrumental object refers back to subject; use the reflexive instr собой.
Лена расскажет о себе. (Lena will tell about herself.) Subject = Лена, prep object refers back to subject; use the reflexive prep о себе.
У неё есть собака. (She has a dog.) 3rd-person personal pronoun after у; н-prefix triggered (Lesson 3).
Маша знает её брата. (Masha knows her brother.) Invariant possessive её (Lesson 4); doesn't decline.

cells: его / её / их do not decline

items.promptEnglish: Anton works with this engineer. (warm-up from Lesson 5)
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 5: с + instr, masc. The этим / этом pair.
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 5: the masc instr of этот is этим (NOT этом, which is the prepositional). С + instr triggers the instrumental form. Today we mix all five lessons and add the reflexive себя.

items.hint: The object refers back to the subject 'я'. Which pronoun is used?
items.explanation: The object refers back to the subject (я → я), so the reflexive pronoun себя is used (acc / gen). Меня would be the regular personal acc, used when the object is someone else (Маша знает меня, where the subject is different).

items.hint: Гордиться + instr; the object refers back to Маша.
items.explanation: Гордиться takes the instrumental, and the object refers back to the subject Маша, so the reflexive instr собой is used. Ей would be the regular 3sg fem instr, used if the object were a different woman.

items.hint: Recap from Lesson 3: у + gen with 3rd-person fem pronoun.
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 3: у + gen with the 3rd-person fem pronoun triggers the н- prefix: её → неё. The bare её would be used after a verb with no preposition (Я знаю её), or as the invariant possessive (её брат).

items.hint: О + prep; the object refers back to Лена. Which form follows о for reflexive prep?
items.explanation: The reflexive pronoun's prepositional form is о себе; the answer is себе alone because the о is already in the sentence. The reflexive is used because the object refers back to the subject Лена.

items.hint: His as a possessive is invariant. The noun брата is the one in the accusative.
items.explanation: Его (his, possessive) is invariant: it does NOT decline. Брата is in the accusative (masc animate, acc = gen), but the possessive его stays его. Compare with Lesson 3: него (with prefix) would be the personal pronoun him after a preposition, NOT the possessive.

blanks: Маша готовит _____ кофе. (Masha is making herself coffee.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Готовить + dat (indirect object: готовить кому); the object refers back to Маша. The reflexive dat is себе. Compare with Маша готовит ей кофе (Masha is making her coffee, where the recipient is a different woman).

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: After the victory Masha is proud of herself.
errorCorrection.explanation: When the object refers back to the subject, Russian uses the reflexive pronoun. Masha is proud of HERSELF, so гордиться (instrumental) takes the reflexive собой, not ей. Ей (and the variant ею) is the regular 3rd-person feminine instrumental, which would mean Masha is proud of some OTHER woman. The reflexive instrumental is собой.

errorCorrection.sentence: Каждое воскресенье Лена ходит к ей в гости.
errorCorrection.explanation: After a preposition, a 3rd-person pronoun takes the н- prefix: к + ей (dative) becomes к ней. К ей leaves the bare form, which only appears without a preposition (помогать ей). The goal of motion after к is к ней.

errorCorrection.sentence: На день рождения Антон купил ему новый телефон.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: For his birthday Anton bought himself a new phone.
errorCorrection.explanation: When the recipient refers back to the subject, Russian uses the reflexive. Anton bought the phone for HIMSELF, so купить (dative recipient) takes the reflexive себе, not ему. Ему is the regular 3rd-person masculine dative, which would mean Anton bought it for some OTHER man. The reflexive dative is себе.

minimalPairs.explanation: The object refers back to the subject (я → я), so the reflexive себя is used. Меня would be used when the object is a different person speaking about me (Антон знает меня).

С + instr with the 3rd-person masc pronoun triggers the н- prefix: им → ним. The bare его would be the acc / gen of the personal pronoun (used without a preposition) or the invariant possessive (which is a different role).

patternRecognition.question: Why is the form него and not его?
options: Lesson 3: 3rd-person personal pronoun after preposition; н- prefix triggered
Lesson 6: reflexive себя in the genitive
patternRecognition.answer: Lesson 3: 3rd-person personal pronoun after preposition; н- prefix triggered
patternRecognition.explanation: У triggers the н- prefix on the 3rd-person masc personal pronoun: его → него. The form is genitive (after у), but the surface change here is the prefix, not the case ending.

patternRecognition.question: Why does его stay the same even though сестру is in the accusative?
options: Lesson 1: acc / gen of он is его
Lesson 3: н- prefix not triggered without preposition
Lesson 4: invariant possessive that never declines, regardless of the noun's case
patternRecognition.answer: Lesson 4: invariant possessive that never declines, regardless of the noun's case
patternRecognition.explanation: Его here is the possessive 'his' (Lesson 4 invariant trio). Possessive его, её, их NEVER decline. Сестру is in the accusative (masc/fem animate); the noun changes form, but the invariant possessive stays as is.

patternRecognition.question: Why is the form собой and not ей?
options: Lesson 4: declined possessive in the instrumental
Lesson 5: declined demonstrative in the instrumental
Lesson 6: reflexive, object refers back to the subject Маша
patternRecognition.answer: Lesson 6: reflexive, object refers back to the subject Маша
patternRecognition.explanation: The object of гордиться refers back to the subject Маша, so the reflexive instr собой is used. Ей would be the regular 3sg fem instr, used if Маша were proud of someone else (e.g. Маша гордится сестрой, where сестра is a different person).

patternRecognition.question: Why is the form этим and not этом?
options: Lesson 3: н- prefix on 3rd-person personal pronoun
Lesson 5: instrumental of demonstrative: с triggers instr, not prep
patternRecognition.answer: Lesson 5: instrumental of demonstrative: с triggers instr, not prep
patternRecognition.explanation: С + instr triggers the instrumental form of the demonstrative этот: этим (NOT этом, which is the prepositional). The этим / этом pair is the trickiest demonstrative slot; the trigger word disambiguates.

reviewVocab.definition: reflexive pronoun (себя: refers back to the subject; has no nominative and no person / gender / number distinctions)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Я знаю себя' слово 'себя' — возвратное местоимение в винительном падеже.

reviewVocab.definition: the five-step pronoun diagnostic (class → case → invariance → preposition → form)
reviewVocab.example: Видна диагностика: класс — личное; падеж — род. падеж; форма склоняемая; предлог есть; форма у него.

reviewVocab.definition: one's own (the reflexive possessive that points back to the subject; declines like мой / твой)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Маша любит свою сестру' местоимение свою согласуется с винительным падежом женского рода.
